clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: A hospital's adult blood-culture contamination rate decreases after a standardized collection initiative. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: Fewer cultures are being classified as probable contaminants, supporting improved collection quality and fewer false-positive results.
options.B: The lower rate proves every bloodstream infection is now detected correctly and other quality measures are unnecessary.
options.C: The contamination rate is unrelated to collection practices and therefore has little quality-improvement value.
options.D: The lower rate means fewer true bloodstream infections are being identified and collection should be less rigorous.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC identifies blood-culture contamination rate as a patient-safety and laboratory-quality measure representing the relative incidence of probable contaminated cultures. CDC recommends monitoring contamination and single-set rates because they provide insight into blood-culture collection practices and reveal gaps that can be targeted for mitigation. False-positive cultures caused by contamination can lead to unnecessary antibiotic therapy and prolonged hospitalization. A lower contamination rate therefore supports improved collection quality and reduced false-positive risk, but it does not prove perfect diagnostic accuracy for all bloodstream infections.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Interpret a lower blood-culture contamination rate as evidence of fewer probable contamination events and improved collection quality without overclaiming complete diagnostic accuracy.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'all' distractor cue, shortened the correct answer, and anchored the interpretation to CDC's current blood-culture contamination quality-measure framework without overclaiming diagnostic completeness.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Blood Culture Contamination quality tool — Overview, Primary Measure, Report and Take Action

audit_findings_append.finding: The original answer was uniquely longest and one distractor overclaimed universal accuracy. The revised item tests the quality-measure interpretation directly with balanced alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. It reflects the CDC definition and quality-improvement use of a lower contamination rate.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. One contamination metric cannot prove perfect detection of every true bloodstream infection or eliminate other quality measures.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. CDC specifically uses contamination monitoring to evaluate and improve blood-culture collection practices.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Contamination refers to false-positive risk, not fewer true bloodstream infections.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone accurately interprets what a lower contamination rate means without exceeding the measure's scope.
cueing_check: All four options are interpretations of the same quality metric and are comparable in length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
